**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scale against the configured checkpoint depth**

When a caller uses a supported custom `num_obs_checkpoints` ladder deeper than 256, this memory-only ratio no longer guarantees that the resulting batch fits. For example, an A10G still receives 3,593 pixels with `num_obs_checkpoints=(512,)`, producing a legal 3,679,232-token sub-batch—well above the documented 2,329,600-token measured ceiling—so deterministic OOM retries and permanent chunk failures remain possible. `_normalize_obs_checkpoints` accepts arbitrary positive depths, so either incorporate the configured maximum into this calculation or reject ladders beyond the calibrated bound.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for packed actors when fitting the batch**

When `config.num_gpus` is fractional, the scheduler deliberately packs multiple actors onto one card, but every actor computes its batch from the card's full memory. For example, two 0.5-GPU actors on an A10G each select 3,593 pixels; at the deepest default bucket each working set is predicted at about 17.1 GiB, so concurrent forwards require roughly 34.2 GiB from a 22.06 GiB card and reintroduce the OOM/retry failure this change is meant to prevent. Fit against the actor's memory share (or disallow fractional reservations for inference) rather than treating every CUDA actor as the sole card occupant.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor fitted capacities below the batch floor**

The fresh evidence relative to the earlier fractional-GPU finding is that the new `MIN_GPU_BATCH_SIZE` clamp can still override the newly added share calculation. With the accepted default ladder and `num_gpus=0.1` on an A10G, the fit is 359 but this line returns 512; Ray can pack ten such actors on the card, producing an aggregate deepest-bucket demand of `512 * 512 * 10 = 2,621,440` tokens, above the documented 2,329,600-token ceiling. Very deep accepted checkpoint ladders have the same problem. Return the lower safe fit, or reject configurations whose safe batch falls below the operational floor, rather than knowingly oversizing them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap requests against the calibrated batch capacity**

When a caller sets the supported `batch_size` field above its 7,168 default, multiplying that request by the card ratio preserves the caller's over-allocation rather than enforcing the calibrated capacity. For example, `batch_size=10_000` with the default ladder on an A10G returns 5,013, whose deepest legal sub-batch is 2,566,656 tokens—above the documented 2,329,600-token ceiling—so this policy can still deterministically OOM without involving the minimum floor. Derive the safe cap from the calibrated 7,168 batch and return the smaller of that cap and the configured request.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scale by the actual packed share of the card**

For fractional reservations that are not exact reciprocals, the reservation is smaller than the memory share each homogeneous inference actor actually receives: `FleetDemand.machines` packs `floor(1 / num_gpus)` actors per card. For example, `num_gpus=0.6` permits only one actor on an L40S, but this line treats it as owning 60% of the card and cuts its otherwise-safe 7,168 batch to about 4,368; at `0.4`, two actors are packed but each is sized to 40% rather than the available 50%. Since the documented measurements identify 7,168 as throughput-optimal, this unnecessarily reduces campaign throughput for accepted configurations. Use the reciprocal of the actual packing count as the share, or reject non-reciprocal reservations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**MEDIUM**
`MIN_GPU_BATCH_SIZE` can exceed the safe batch computed above. For example, an allowed `num_obs_checkpoints=(4096,)` on an A10G computes about 224 but returns 512, yielding 4,194,304 tokens—well above the documented 2,329,600-token ceiling. Small fractional reservations have the same problem. Reject unsupported configurations or allow batches below 512 when required for safety.
